definition_written_here_DEF_A4_ARGUED.binding: for Ezekiel now; proposed to method section 17 as the cross-book definition
definition_written_here_DEF_A4_ARGUED.1_argued_citation: Any verse anchor a prose field carries — an Ezek.C.V token with or without witness prefix, a bare C:V cite, an 'MT C:V' qualifier, or a v. / vv. / verse(s) N expression resolved against a single-chapter span — together with the assertion it anchors. Fields scanned: every string field except SKIP_KEYS (unchanged).
definition_written_here_DEF_A4_ARGUED.2_unit: A dash-range is one citation; a comma / 'and' list is one citation per member; repeated citation of the same verse-set in one row is one citation.
definition_written_here_DEF_A4_ARGUED.3_mirrored: A citation is mirrored when a boundary_evidence_refs entry covers its verse, or, for a range, covers either endpoint or the whole range, compared in WEB space after witness conversion.
definition_written_here_DEF_A4_ARGUED.4_defect: Every unmirrored citation with at least one verse inside the A4 window [first-1, last+1] is a worklist item; a citation wholly outside the window is far-side: recorded, never a defect (#e12 A4).
definition_written_here_DEF_A4_ARGUED.5_no_narrowing_to_evidentiary: 'Argued' is NOT narrowed to 'argued as evidence'. Under OW-18 a verse anchor is an assertion about the witness at that verse, and the refs list is the row's checkable index of such assertions; the rows already practise this (P07-001 mirrors 29:4 'not argued as boundary evidence'; P08-002 mirrors 33:20 'disclosed, never argued as a boundary'). The member judges mirroring; it never judges weight. Enforce in the tool what the tool can measure (OW-18); put the judgement where a person writes it and a reviewer reads it.
definition_written_here_DEF_A4_ARGUED.6_role_token_mandatory: Every installed entry carries one fixed ROLE token, then free text under the rotation rule (at least 4 formulations, at most 6 words): WARRANT-onset | WARRANT-close | WARRANT-rival (the A9/A16 rival weighed) | WARRANT-absence-over-range (the 'no formula / mark / K-Q inside C:V-C:V' claims) | DISCLOSURE-kq | DISCLOSURE-mark | DISCLOSURE-paseq | DISCLOSURE-note | DISCLOSURE-device (an in-span device the boundary does not rest on) | QUOTE (an A6 run anchored here) | ANCHOR (a content or structural statement the boundary does not rest on; the rows' existing 'not argued as boundary evidence'). The token is what the spot wave checks: a WARRANT token on a verse the rationale does not rest on is a defect; an ANCHOR token is never a boundary claim. Existing entries are NOT re-tokenised in this wave; the vocabulary applies to installs.
definition_written_here_DEF_A4_ARGUED.7_why_not_option_2: The member is a Tier-0 gate. Installing the peers' 47 and keeping the member 'as a net' leaves about 145 in-span citations flagging at the close gate unless the rule is changed — and the rule is A4, which R1 confirmed. An end state in which the gate is red and the worklist is done is not a choice; it is a deferred contradiction.
definition_written_here_DEF_A4_ARGUED.8_why_not_narrowing: MEASURED above: the class a narrowing would remove is about five entries, and no mechanical test separates them from the Hebrew-quoted, rival-seam and absence claims around them without a judgement the tool cannot make (peer_11's A4 finding). The cost of the honest rule is a handful of ANCHOR entries; the cost of the narrowing is a tool that encodes a judgement it cannot audit.
